system_description.narrative_title: A Fracturing Global Order: Markets, Wars, and Strategic Economic Warfare
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an open, tightly coupled system in flux where economic policy, financial markets, and regional wars reciprocally amplify shocks. U.S. domestic politics and aggressive economic-statecraft (sanctions, asset seizures, control of energy resources) are colliding with a hawkish pivot in central banking, producing volatile capital flows and higher borrowing costs. Simultaneously, protracted kinetic conflicts (Iran, Ukraine) and supply‑side shocks (energy, grain, logistics) are accelerating realignments—China expanding leverage, Europe and allies hedging, and emergent de‑dollarisation and industrial reshoring pressures rising.
system_description.scope: State actors and alliances; central banks, sovereign treasuries and capital markets; sanctions and trade policy instruments; global energy, food and critical‑minerals flows; multinational corporations and supply chains; conflict theatres (Iran war, Russia–Ukraine) and their geopolitical spillovers.
system_description.super_system: The globalized political‑economic system (planetary international order of states, markets, institutions and transnational infrastructure).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system (sovereign bond markets, central banking, capital flows)
Global energy and commodity subsystem (oil, gas, grain, logistics networks)
Regional security subsystems (Middle East conflict theatre; Europe–Russia front; Indo‑Pacific balance)

variables.name: U.S.–Iran military and economic confrontation
variables.description: The United States, Iran and Gulf actors are locked in an escalating mix of strikes, naval engagements and broad economic coercion that is shifting how regional force and pressure are applied.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and European security escalation
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed politically and materially by NATO and EU states, are seeing intensifying kinetic strikes and 'gray‑zone' operations that are deepening Europe's defense burdens and military posture.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic, trade and technology rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting industrial and strategic advantage through tighter trade measures, export controls and competition in advanced technologies, shifting global supply chains and standards.

variables.name: Global financial repricing and monetary stress
variables.description: A sharp repricing in global bond markets tied to hawkish U.S. policy and rising sovereign borrowing costs is straining capital flows, testing central bank–fiscal boundaries and reshaping investors' risk calculus worldwide.

variables.name: Energy geopolitics and oil asset reallocation
variables.description: Disruptions from Middle East conflict and strategic moves by major powers to secure crude supplies and stakes abroad are redistributing oil sources and weakening traditional producer blocs' influence.
